trial_court: Court of Subordinate Judge, Madanapalle - O.S. No.168 of 1981
case_name: S. Yellamma And Ors. vs S. Anjaneyulu And Anr.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: S. Yellamma And Ors. (wife and daughters)
parties.respondent_defendant: S. Anjaneyulu And Anr. (husband and another person)

facts_of_case: The first plaintiff and the first defendant lived together with their children until two months prior to filing the suit. The first defendant joined hands with the second defendant, who poisoned the mind of the first plaintiff. The first plaintiff filed a suit for maintenance at Rs.300/-per month and marriage expenses for plaintiffs 2 and 3 at Rs.30,000/-each. The trial court dismissed the suit on the ground that the first defendant is not guilty of desertion or abandonment of the first plaintiff.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu wife is entitled to maintenance whether or not the husband possesses property.
legal_principles.held: As per Hindu customary law as well as Statute law, maintenance of wife by her husband is a matter of personal obligation arising from the very existence of the relationship.

legal_principles.principle: A statement made by a party having proprietary interest in the subject-matter of appeal is an admission which suggests an inference to the fact in issue.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 18 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, a statement made by a party having proprietary interest in the subject-matter of appeal is an admission which suggests an inference to the fact in issue.

outcome.final_order: The final court order was in favor of the petitioners, allowing their appeal against the trial court's decision to dismiss the suit.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in family law disputes
